ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The central atom in the figure is a carbon, connected to two substituents R¹ and R²; the same central carbon is also connected to a positively charged H2O/OH2 group and to an azide fragment. The azide group starts from the carbon end as N, a positively charged middle N, and a negatively charged terminal N; the figure also has curved arrows and dashed-line/transition-state representations, but the problem requires ignoring the arrows. Reasoning: According to the specified method, treat R¹ and R² as two wildcard substituents `*`; write the positively charged water/oxonium substituent as `[OH2+]` and connect it to the central carbon; write the azide group in the cumulative double-bond form as `N=[N+]=[N-]`, with the first N connected to the central carbon. Therefore, combining them gives the SMILES: `*C(*)([OH2+])N=[N+]=[N-]`.

method.method_draft: First parse only the chemical skeleton in the image, not the arrows. Treat R1 and R2 as two wildcard substituents on the central carbon. Add the positively charged water/oxonium substituent as `[OH2+]` attached to that carbon. Then add the azide substituent from the carbon through neutral N to positively charged middle N and negatively charged terminal N, using the shown cumulated double-bond form. Combine these into the SMILES `*C(*)([OH2+])N=[N+]=[N-]`.
